relevance_note: Single-patient report of SSADH deficiency with 20-year follow-up: 'Here we report the case history and follow-up for one of the earliest-diagnosed patients with SSADH deficiency', giving individual-level detail (sex, ages, features, treatment) for that person.
method_note: Case report (letter), no data tables (only Figure 1, a schematic diagram), so no table transcription was needed and no stacked cells occur; no per-patient reference column. One in-scope person: the single unnamed patient, labelled 'patient' (rule 5); the paper's 'our patient'/'The patient' is a role word, not a label. The paper prints no variant description anywhere (no cDNA, protein or genomic string; the diagnosis was biochemical: 'SSADH deficiency was documented in peripheral blood leucocytes'), so the variants table has one placeholder row with variant_original_string 'not reported' as the v3 rule requires; no zygosity, inheritance, ACMG or functional data exist. Gene symbol recorded as printed in the body text ('Aldh5a1'; the form 'ALDH5a1' appears only in reference [10]). Publications.cites_prior_report_of_same_patients = true: reference [9] is cited at the sentence documenting her diagnosis ('...at that time.9'), and ref [9] is the earlier report of this same patient (Gibson KM, Hoffmann G, Nyhan WL, 1988, Eur J Pediatr, PMID:3409929); prior_report_citation is that reference line. Contradiction/ambiguity found: ref [9]'s title states 'in a patient without ataxia or convulsions', but I did not use a cited reference title as phenotype evidence, so ataxia is excluded only from the in-text statement 'Appendicular and truncal coordination appeared normal.' and 'seizures or epilepsy' is left 'not reported'. Group statements about the disease (the phenotype list in the introduction and the neurobehavioral list in the Discussion) are not about this patient and were not used as her features. Normal findings recorded as exclusions per D-27: coordination normal -> 'ataxia' excluded; muscle strength normal -> 'muscle weakness' excluded; MRI 'normal T_l, T_2, and balanced-pulse sequences' -> 'T2 hyperintensity ... on MRI' excluded (the investigation names the T2 sequence); 'Sleep schedule is normal' -> 'sleep disturbance' excluded, although the same sentence adds 'occasional extended sleep periods last 12 to 15 hours' (not called abnormal). The parents appear only as 'Parental consent was provided' and in the acknowledgements with no individual-level facts, so no relative rows were created. All spans were copied character for character from the Markdown and checked to occur verbatim.
